title: CIRTL National Presents: Teaching with Objects – An Eﬀective Teaching Method for Future Faculty
description: This interactive workshop is designed to equip graduate students and future faculty with the foundational skills and confidence to integrate object-based learning into their teaching across all disciplines. Moving beyond the misconception that object-based pedagogy is confined to art history or requires special expertise, this session introduces participants to the "See/Think/Wonder" framework—a versatile tool for facilitating evidence-based, student-centered discussion that can be applied in STEM, humanities, social sciences, and beyond. Participants will learn to design effective assignments, practice leading object-based discussions, and navigate campus resources and expert collaborations. The workshop emphasizes that effective teaching with objects relies not on the instructor's pre-existing content knowledge, but on their skill as a facilitator of observation and critical inquiry—a transferable skill applicable to any classroom setting. Optional pre-reading materials and a simple framework guide will be provided in advance to ensure all participants can engage meaningfully, regardless of prior experience. This session is ideal for anyone looking to create more engaged, interdisciplinary, and experiential learning environments in their future classrooms. By the end of this workshop, participants will be prepared to: Articulate the core philosophy of object-based learning as a student-centered, evidence-based pedagogical approach applicable beyond the arts and humanities Apply the "See/Think/Wonder" thinking routine to structure an object-based learning activity that fosters observation, interpretation, and questioning Design a scaffolded discussion prompt that uses an object to advance a specific learning goal in their discipline

title: Demystifying Service-Learning: Elevating Workforce Readiness Through Public-Impact Projects
description: True workforce readiness requires more than technical competency—modern employers are actively seeking graduates who can navigate ambiguity, collaborate across differences, and solve complex community challenges. In fact, the AAC&U national employer report (The Agility Imperative) reveals that 76% of employers are more likely to hire graduates with community-based project experience, and 94% view citizenship development and workforce preparation as a single, unified goal. This introductory session explores how service-learning bridges the gap between student career readiness and real-world problem-solving. We will examine how to conceptualize service-learning partnerships that are deeply reciprocal, mutually beneficial, and sustainable for both faculty and community stakeholders. This foundational workshop is designed to pique your interest and shift your perspective. You will leave with a clear roadmap and direct access to CTE consultation support. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify key components of reciprocal service-learning partnerships that align with workforce readiness.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

Participants will explore recording options using the desktop application and web recorder, learn how to organize and share videos, and gain a basic understanding of Panopto's built-in editing tools. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify key Panopto features available for recording, managing, and sharing course media. 2) Demonstrate how to create and publish recordings using the Panopto desktop application and web recorder. 3) Apply basic editing functions to enhance recorded content.

This foundational workshop is designed to pique your interest and shift your perspective. You will leave with a clear roadmap and direct access to CTE consultation support. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify key components of reciprocal service-learning partnerships that align with workforce readiness.

title: Beyond AI Summaries: Collaborative Reading with Perusall
description: As GenAI makes it easier than ever for students to bypass the intellectual work of reading, instructors face new challenges in designing meaningful learning experiences around course texts. This workshop demonstrates how Perusall can turn reading assignments into interactive learning communities where students collaboratively interpret ideas, challenge assumptions, and learn from one another. Participants will explore assignment design strategies and Perusall features that promote deeper engagement, accountability, and authentic learning. title: Write Line Group B Fall 2026
description: The purpose of Write Line is to provide a productive virtual writing space so you can stay accountable to your writing goals. As a Write Line participant, you’ll commit to meeting with a small virtual writing group via Zoom once per week for 2 and a half hours each session. Group B will meet on Mondays at 2:00 until 4:30pm. Each group will have a UWC facilitator who will briefly introduce a writing concept and inquire about their writing goals for the session. Then, everyone will write! Participants who have quick writing questions will be able to get answers to those via the Zoom chat function. At the end of each session, small groups will briefly reconvene to report on their progress. If you have questions, contact Lauren at lmcauliffe@tamu.edu. Groups that are already full are full, and we will not add additional participants beyond the 30-person limit. You will receive a Zoom link and more information the day or two before the start time, not in the ERS confirmation email.

title: From Submission to Demonstrated Learning with Peerceptiv
description: In a world where GenAI tools can influence how students complete assignments, instructors seek additional ways to evaluate student learning beyond the final submission. This workshop explores Peerceptiv's peer assessment ecosystem with a focus on creating opportunities for students to explain, discuss, and defend their work. Participants will examine how structured peer feedback and a live presentation can promote accountability, meaningful engagement, and authentic demonstrations of learning while supporting a variety of instructional approaches to GenAI. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Explain why peer assessment remains a valuable strategy for promoting feedback, critical thinking, and demonstrated learning even with GenAI available. 2) Evaluate how Peerceptiv features, such as peer review, Integrity Check, and Live Presentations can be used to increase transparency of student work, encourage accountability, and provide additional evidence of student learning. 3) Design a Peerceptiv assessment strategy that integrates peer feedback, Integrity Check, and Live Presentations to promote authentic participation, meaningful evaluation, and demonstrated learning.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: Conversation Circle for English Language Proficiency
description: Conversation Circle is a supportive space for practicing spoken English through group discussions on cultural topics, including American university culture. The sessions promote social connections, intercultural dialogue, and a sense of belonging. The goal is to enhance English fluency, comprehension, and confidence. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to: 1. Employ effective spontaneous communication skills in social, academic and professional settings. 2. Apply appropriate turn-taking and active listening techniques in casual group discussions and more formal academic discussions.

title: Workshop: Dude, what’s your problem? Understanding problem framing to achieve good solutions.
description: All of us want to solve problems, and many of us pursue professional and civic pathways focused on problem-solving, whether that’s politics, engineering, business, or many, many other pursuits. However, we’re often not aware of the crucial step of problem-framing and how it determines the types of potential solutions that might be generated and their eventual success (or failure). In this workshop, participants will identify problems that plague their lives, look at past cases of effective and ineffective problem-framing and problem-solving, and consider how the problems they’ve identified can be framed to achieve different outcomes. The importance of this process will be underscored with applications in government, technology, business, and other fields.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: Workshop: Think Before You Click: A Look at Image Verification
description: They say a picture can speak a thousand words, if only those words were all true. In this age of misinformation, AI slop and doom scrolling it’s become easier than ever to consume images online that are misleading, mislabeled or completely false. This workshop will review basic image verification techniques by placing the audience in real breaking news scenarios. Participants will experience in real time how easy it is to share a bogus image and learn how to confirm its authenticity before hitting click.

description: The purpose of Write Line is to provide a productive virtual writing space so you can stay accountable to your writing goals. As a Write Line participant, you’ll commit to meeting with a small virtual writing group via Zoom once per week for 2 and a half hours each session. Group A will meet on Wednesdays at 12:00 until 2:30pm. Each group will have a UWC facilitator who will briefly introduce a writing concept and inquire about their writing goals for the session. Then, everyone will write! Participants who have quick writing questions will be able to get answers to those via the Zoom chat function. At the end of each session, small groups will briefly reconvene to report on their progress. If you have questions, contact Lauren at lmcauliffe@tamu.edu. title: Conversation Circle for English Language Proficiency
description: Conversation Circle is a supportive space for practicing spoken English through group discussions on cultural topics, including American university culture. Participants improve spontaneous speaking, active listening, and conversational turn-taking. Through communication with speakers from a variety of backgrounds, they acclimate to different accents. The sessions promote social connections, intercultural dialogue, and a sense of belonging. The goal is to enhance English fluency, comprehension, and confidence. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to: 1. Employ effective spontaneous communication skills in social, academic and professional settings. 2. Apply appropriate turn-taking and active listening techniques in casual group discussions and more formal academic discussions.

description: Second in a series of workshops for graduate students, post-docs, and visiting scholars whose primary language is not English. This interactive workshop provides instructors and public speakers with functional vocabulary for describing a visual aid aloud. It promotes comprehensible speech by teaching the importance of stressing the correct syllable within a word, how to stress a syllable (in terms of pitch, volume, length, and vowel quality), and how to know which syllable to stress. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to... 1.Describe a visual aid from your major aloud to a peer, using the recommended framework. 2.Identify polysyllabic words from your major. 3.Produce stress on the target syllable.

title: Providing Students Multiple Pathways to Demonstrate Mastery
description: The design of an assessment can affect how students demonstrate what they know and whether they have equal access to the assessment. By applying the principles of Universal Design for Learning (UDL), instructors can create flexible assessments that reduce barriers; emphasize authentic demonstrations of learning; and maintain rigorous academic expectations. In partnership with Justin Romack, Assistant Director at the Disability Resources Office, this workshop explores how assessment design influences student access and success. It examines common barriers students encounter in traditional assessments and discusses practical strategies for designing assessments that provide multiple pathways for students to demonstrate their learning. Participants will also discover how generative AI can support brainstorming alternative assessment formats, applying UDL principles to assessments, and simplifying assignment language. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify common barriers in traditional assessment design that may limit student access and opportunities to demonstrate learning. 2) Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles to design or revise assessments. 3) Identify ways generative AI can assist with creating alternative assessment formats and redesigning assessments.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: Workshop: Confronting McCarthyism: Evaluating Evidence as a Historian
description: What does it mean to be a “patriotic” American? How do we define “loyalty” to the nation? And who establishes the standards for allegiance in a democratic society? Using the 1950s’ House Un-American Activities Committee proceedings as a framework, this session explores how we can learn from history when evaluating arguments over national identity and patriotism. Participants will assess how information is used to substantiate arguments and explore how historians critically evaluate evidence for authenticity, bias, and authority.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: Conversation Circle for English Language Proficiency
description: Conversation Circle is a supportive space for practicing spoken English through group discussions on cultural topics, including American university culture. Participants improve spontaneous speaking, active listening, and conversational turn-taking. Through communication with speakers from a variety of backgrounds, they acclimate to different accents. The sessions promote social connections, intercultural dialogue, and a sense of belonging. The goal is to enhance English fluency, comprehension, and confidence. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to: 1. Employ effective spontaneous communication skills in social, academic and professional settings. 2. Elaborate on their viewpoints and opinions in group discussions. 3. Construct clear and well-structured responses during impromptu conversations. 4. Apply appropriate turn-taking and active listening techniques in casual group discussions and more formal academic discussions.

title: NACADA Webinar: Deconstructing Burnout in Advising: Reframing Solutions from Self-Care to Prevention
description: This session will explore, unpack, and deconstruct burnout through perspectives and experiences of advisors from various geographic and institutional settings. Advising work may be close to our hearts, but there’s a limit to how much space and energy one can give when passion, a student focus, and self-care are inadequate to prevent burnout. Framed by the 12 stages of burnout and the concept of emotional labor, panelists will examine how higher education fosters certain types of burnout that impact advisors and the profession. Participants will be encouraged to consider their spheres of influence as advisors, managers, and colleagues as we seek to interrupt, intervene, and reframe burnout to address its root causes and learn how the profession can support advisors in this era of change. Participants will be able to: - Identify the symptoms and stages of burnout. - Recognize the impact of burnout on advisors and the profession. - Examine ways of preventing or minimizing burnout rather than relying on self-care. - Understand how to create strategies to help prevent burnout.

title: American English Vowel System (Part 1 of 4)
description: The vowel sounds of American English are challenging to learners of English because there are so many, and because English spelling does not convey the pronunciation predictably. This four-session series of interactive workshops aims to increase attendees' phonological awareness, and as a result, their listening and intelligibility. Through a variety of activities and handouts, attendees will become familiar with each vowel and with resources to practice listening discrimination and pronunciation on their own. Each attendee has the opportunity to get personalized feedback on their own pronunciation. title: NACADA Webinar: The Art of Saying No: Navigating Difficult Academic Advising Conversations
description: Difficult conversations are an inevitable part of academic advising, but they often come with a heavy emotional toll. Whether delivering disappointing news about academic policies, discussing a student's poor performance, or addressing issues like academic dismissal, these challenging interactions can lead to burnout and emotional exhaustion. In this webinar, we aim to equip academic advisors with practical tools and strategies to navigate these tough conversations while managing their emotional well-being. Utilizing Compassionate Directness, the SPIKES protocol, and BRIGHT advising approach, we address the art of saying "no." At the end the webinar, we aim for participants to have actionable insights, self-reflection tools, and self-care strategies designed to enhance their ability to handle challenging conversations and create a healthier, more effective advising environment. Participants will be able to: - Identify personal strengths and areas for improvement in handling difficult conversations, based on self-assessment of common advising scenarios. - Demonstrate the ability to apply at least three effective communication strategies for difficult conversations, including techniques for saying no assertively, through worksheet and role-play exercises. - Create a self-care plan that includes strategies to maintain well-being when engaging in difficult conversations and creating a supportive advising environment.

title: Workshop: Leading with Integrity: Giving and Receiving Criticism
description: It’s hard to receive criticism without feeling defensive, ashamed, or angry, and it’s hard to give criticism without worrying about damaging your relationships. As a result, we don’t give criticism even when we know that we should, and we don’t learn from criticism that could have helped us grow. For groups, organizations, and leaders who value honesty and accountability, this is a serious problem, but there are steps that we can take to both give and receive criticism with greater ease and effectiveness.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is performance or entertainment focused.

title: Workshop: When Loyalties Collide: What Does It Mean to Lead in an Era of Conflicting Loyalties?
description: Our loyalties profoundly shape how we interpret events, information, and people, often in ways we don't recognize. Studies consistently show that two people with different loyalties can witness the same situation and reach completely opposite conclusions. This makes it essential for leaders to critically examine their own loyalties: Why are we loyal to certain ideas, people, or groups? Are these loyalties justified? When should we reconsider or even abandon a loyalty? In this workshop we will explore various definitions and theories of loyalty, which will help you to develop practical frameworks for navigating conflicting loyalties and leading with moral clarity.

title: CIRTL National Presents: UDL + AI Design Studio
description: The UDL + AI Design Studio is a seven-week redesign studio where instructors improve one real teaching challenge using Universal Design for Learning (UDL)—a widely recognized, research-grounded framework for designing learning experiences. While UDL is highly respected in higher education, it is often presented as a complex set of principles and strategies; this studio reframes it as a simple, practical WHY–WHAT–HOW design cycle that makes redesign manageable and actionable. AI functions as a design partner, helping instructors apply UDL more efficiently to refine activities and assessments with clarity and precision. By the end of this short course, participants will be prepared to: Analyze a specific teaching challenge using baseline evidence to identify where students struggle and what factors are contributing to the problem Apply the UDL Learning Design Cycle (WHY → WHAT → HOW), using AI as a design assistant to generate, refine, and stress-test UDL-informed design moves efficiently Create a cohesive UDL + AI redesign package that strengthens student engagement, improves content clarity or access, and supports meaningful performance Evaluate the redesign by developing a feasible implementation and evidence plan that identifies indicators of impact and next steps for refinement.

title: CIRTL National Presents: Designing Assignments with UDL: Supporting Student Emotional Capacity
description: This workshop utilizes an object-based teaching and learning approach, allowing participants to engage with and learn directly from assignments from a wide range of disciplines. In the first session, participants will use authentic assignments as shared objects for observation, analysis, and discussion to uncover assumptions they may hold about students' emotional capacity before connecting those observations and assumptions to the UDL framework and UDL informed assignment design strategies. At the end of this session participants will begin to redesign an assignment relevant to their discipline by using at least one of the assignment design strategies discussed in the session. In the second session, participants will explore action-oriented feedback as a tool for maintaining motivation and promoting growth, then participate in a structured peer-review process to refine their assignment revisions. Participants will leave with a deeper understanding of how assignment design influences students' emotional experiences and concrete strategies for designing assignments that better support the emotional needs of learners. By the end of this workshop, participants will be prepared to: Discuss concrete strategies for promoting student emotional capacity through incorporating UDL considerations 8.5, and 9.1-3 in assignment design. Design or revise an assignment to promote student emotional capacity through the incorporation of one or more of the UDL emotional capacity considerations.

Identify situations in academic and instructional communication where accurate grammar is essential for conveying meaning clearly. 2. Produce appropriate grammatical structures in spoken English, applying individualized feedback to improve accuracy and comprehensibility. 3. Monitor and revise their own spoken grammar while communicating in academic and professional contexts.

title: CIRTL National Presents: Exploring Teaching Careers at Teaching Intensive Universities with CIRTL Alumni
description: In this online panel, we'll hear from CIRTL alumni who now teach at liberal arts colleges. title: ELP Special Topics in Grammar for Speech
description: Do you have questions about English grammar that haven't been covered in a workshop or need additional practice with a challenging grammar topic? Special Topics in Grammar for Speech is an interactive drop-in session where participants can ask questions about grammar for spoken communication and receive individualized guidance. Discussions may focus on topics such as verb tenses, modal verbs, question formation, articles, passive voice, or any other grammar questions participants bring. Practice activities will be tailored to attendees' needs, providing opportunities to apply new learning by practicing speaking using realistic scenarios. The goal is to enhance grammatical accuracy, spoken fluency, and confidence. Participants will be able to: 1. Identify situations in academic and instructional communication where accurate grammar is essential for conveying meaning clearly. 2. Produce appropriate grammatical structures in spoken English, applying individualized feedback to improve accuracy and comprehensibility. 3. Monitor and revise their own spoken grammar while communicating in academic and professional contexts.

title: NACADA Webinar: Expand Your Toolbox: Integrating Academic Advising and Career Coaching
description: As career readiness and professional skill development become top priorities for higher education, the need for an integrated approach to academic advising and career coaching has never been greater. Advisors are increasingly being called upon to support students not just academically, but in preparing them for meaningful careers beyond graduation. By skillfully incorporating career-focused discussions into existing advising practices, advisors can play a key role in a student's academic and professional success. Through this dynamic webinar, participants will learn how to utilize an integrated advising approach to bolster students’ development by facilitating connections between academic requirements and the cultivation of valuable career readiness competencies. Grounded in practical experience and shared examples, this session provides attendees with the strategies, tools, and resources needed to build their confidence and expand their skillsets. Participants Will be Able To: - Identify ways academic advising, across different student populations, can be enhanced by incorporating career-focused discussions into traditional advising interactions, thus leading to students’ professional success and fulfillment. - Explore areas within current practices in which career-focused discussions can be implemented. - Leverage strategies, tools, and resources to confidently integrate career coaching conversations into advising practices - Develop a plan for fostering a holistic, career-integrated advising environment at their institution
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: NACADA Webinar: From Chaos to Clarity: Building Scalable Advising Systems for Large Caseloads
description: Large advising caseloads are an increasing reality across higher education, often creating tension between operational demands and advisor well-being. As practitioner literature and national conversations continue to highlight the connection between high-volume caseloads and advisor burnout, institutions are seeking structured and sustainable solutions. This webinar explores how advising units can intentionally align operational efficiency with practices that protect advisor capacity while maintaining high-quality student support. Drawing on experiences within an advising center serving undergraduate business students at a large public institution, presenters will outline scalable strategies that promote clarity, consistency, and shared responsibility. Participants will examine structured appointment models, including required versus optional advising touchpoints, as well as tiered advising approaches such as individual, group, and walk-in formats. Presenters will also share cross-team support systems designed to address uneven caseload distribution. In addition, the session will explore advising delivery formats that support accessibility and efficiency, with examples drawn from our in-person and email advising models. The webinar will further highlight the role of standardized documentation practices, centralized resource hubs, and clearly defined advising boundaries in reducing redundancy and preventing burnout. Emphasis will be placed on practical frameworks that can be adapted to institutions of varying sizes and resources levels. Participants will leave with actionable strategies for designing advising systems that balance efficiency with advisor well-being in large caseload environments. Participants Will Be Able To: - Assess structural factors within their advising units that contribute to inefficiency or advisor burnout in large caseload environments. - Design structured appointment models that align required advising touchpoints with institutional capacity and student needs. - Apply tiered advising approaches (e.g., individual, group, and walk-in formats) to improve scalability and resource allocation. - Develop cross-team support systems and standardized documentation practices that promote clarity, shared responsibility, and consistency. - Establish sustainable boundaries and operational practices that protect advisor well-being while maintaining high-quality student support.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: CIRTL National Presents: A Student-Centered Approach to Plagiarism in the Age of Generative AI
description: Many instructors have struggled to address plagiarism in the rise of generative AI, but these technologies may simply be revealing long‑standing gaps in how students understand the work of learning. This two‑part workshop explores how transparency about the cognitive work required in assignments and how students perceive that work can strengthen assessment validity and reduce the reliance of AI in coursework. By the end of this workshop, participants will be able to: Identify the current literature regarding why students plagiarize. Discuss the differences between assessment security and assessment validity. Examine a class assessment's cognitive load, germane load, and extraneous cognitive load. Revise a class assessment to improve its assessment validity and clarify the learning process.

title: GSPDT: Creating Accessible PDFs and Canvas Courses
description: The recent Title II revision (the Final Rule) mandates that all digital content meet accessibility standards, ensuring usability for all learners. This workshop focuses on two key areas of digital accessibility: PDF documents and Canvas course design. PDF files are often the most challenging materials to remediate, and participants will explore common accessibility issues found in PDFs while practicing with Adobe Acrobat’s built-in accessibility checker. The session will also introduce accessibility tools in Canvas, including the platform’s accessibility checker and the Ally report. Participants will learn how to interpret accessibility feedback, apply recommended fixes, and improve the overall accessibility of their course content. Learning Outcomes: Participants will be able to… 1) Identify common accessibility issues found in PDF documents and explain why they create barriers for learners. 2) Use Adobe Acrobat’s accessibility checker to evaluate and remediate PDF files. 3) Apply accessibility best practices within Canvas, including the use of the platform’s accessibility checker. 4) Interpret Ally reports and implement recommended improvements to enhance the accessibility of course materials.

title: NACADA Webinar: Practical Strategies for Trauma-Informed Advising
description: As advisors, students frequently reveal the traumatic events of their lives to us. Without professional licensure in mental health services, what should advisors do? For students to access resources that will address their mental health needs, they first need to reveal to a trusted person that they need help. For this reason, it is incredibly important for advisors to know how to use trauma-informed practices to create a safe space for all students to ask for help. At the basis of trauma-informed advising is intentionally enacting the 5 principles of trauma-informed care in our advising practice, including safety, trustworthiness, choice, collaboration, and empowerment” “Harris & Fallot, 2001”. All of these principles are relational skills at their core, highlighting the importance of relational advising strategies when working with students who have experienced trauma. While the practice of trauma-informed advising is primarily relational, it is often difficult to know how to practically enact trauma-informed conversational strategies with students during high-stress advising moments. This session is ideal for advisors who desire to deepen their understanding of trauma and its impact on students, while learning powerful conversational techniques to better empathize with students in distress. Participants Will Be Able To: - Identify what trauma is, how it impacts our stress-response system, and signs of a student in distress. - Use conversational techniques such as validation, scaling questions, externalization, and parts language to empathize with students while also maintaining appropriate boundaries. - Enact practical strategies for taking a trauma-informed and person-centered approach in our work as advisors. - Make effective referrals to mental health services.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.

title: NACADA Webinar: Advising Undecided Reimagined: Framework, Praxis, and Storytelling for Exploring Stu
description: In 2023 the First Year Advising Center and Career and Life Design at Oakland University were tasked with coming up with a strategy to better support and retain our Undecided (Exploring) student population. Our division leadership created an initiative to develop better lines of communication between departments and to model effective collaboration in a common goal of retaining and supporting this unique student population. Early on our goal was to define the overarching reason we did not retain our Exploring student population at the same rate as their peers. In the years following the initial pilot program we developed resources, strengthened campus partnerships, and best practices for academic advisers and career coaches. These resources have evolved over time and we are excited to share what has proven to be most effective. This session will provide a brief overview of how we built the foundation of our program along with highlighting strategies our colleagues across campus can use to help guide students in the decision making process for major selection. You will learn and practice three unique techniques designed to better support and engage Exploring and Redeciding students. Participants Will Be Able To: - Learn how one advising office leveraged campus partnerships to create and maintain institutional buy-in for a new initiative. - Understand how collaboration with the Career and Life Design Center led to a stronger referral process, increased communication and outreach for students, and more congruent one-stop services. - Use research to create advising tools, resources, and new techniques that helped build new adviser training models. - Understand how Advisors approached building new appointment structures and the content in each student appointment. - Understand how to track student progress data and use it effectively. - Understand why changing the culture and stigma of being Undecided (Exploring) matters for this generation of college students. - Practice advising resources, and techniques that have been successful over the past three years via storytelling, dreaming and brainstorming.
classification_reasoning_summary: Event is academic, research, or career oriented.
